newsitem.title: INDIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - August 1.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - August 1.

text.p: (Prepared by New Delhi-based Business News and Information
Services Pvt Ltd. for Reuters. Telephone no. 11-332-4842,
biznis@giasbm01.vsnl.net.in)
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch
for their accuracy.
TOP STORIES
The Hindustan Times
VETTING OF MEMBERS BY INTELLIGENCE BUREAU ROCKS PARLIAMENT

Prime Minister Gujral told agitated members in the upper house of parliament that his government had not asked the Intelligence Bureau to keep surveillance on Members of Parliament (MPs) or snoop around in parliament house.

A newspaper Thursday morning reported that Intelligence Bureau undercover agents were spying on MPs in and around parliament. The government in an official release said the intelligence officers were deployed to help parliament officials in anti-sabotage checks and other inter-linked duties.
The Times Of India
GOVERNMENT MAY SLASH PROPOSED QUOTA FOR WOMEN

The government has sought the opinion of women ministers and MPs in slashing the proposed quota for women in the lower house of parliament and state assemblies to 20 percent or 25 percent from 33 percent.

The suggestion to reduce the quota came from Prime Minister Gujral and is believed to have been conveyed to women members by Speaker P.A. Sangma. The government feels that unless women parliamentarians agree to a reduced quota, the bill will be derailed again because of the opposition to it.
KEY BUSINESS STORIES
The Economic Times
TAX BREAKS FOR INFRASTRUCTURE SECTOR

The government on Thursday approved a five-year tax holiday to the power, the petroleum and the transport sectors. The announcement is the latest in a series of government initiatives to boost private domestic and overseas investments in the infrastructure sector.
A nodal body under the Industrial Development Bank was recently constituted to go into the financing problems of various private players in the infrastructure sector.
SONY INDIA FACING COMPETITION FROM SONY JAPAN

In its third year of operations, Sony India is competing with overseas Sony colour televisions. The grey market turnover of smuggled Sony televisions pegged at five billion rupees is much more than that of Sony India's which was only 3.43 billion rupees last year.
Financial Express
BOURSE REGULATOR FINALISES NORMS
The bourse regulator the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) has completed the procedure of consolidation and rationalisation of guidelines for disclosure and investor protection.
The draft document includes the eligibility norms for companies accessing the capital markets, the promoter's contribution and the lock-in period.

SEBI has sought comments on its draft from the Association of Merchant Bankers. The draft says unlisted companies are eligible to enter the capital market if it meets the stipulated payment of dividend for the immediately preceding three years.
SUGGESTION TO RAISE DEPRECIATION VALUE OF SHIPS

A committee has recommended raising the depreciation value of ships to 33 percent from 20 percent to attract private investors and overseas companies to the shipping industry. The committee was set up by the Ministry of Surface Transport to formulate a comprehensive shipping policy.

Other recommendations of the committee include export-oriented industry status to the shipping industry, separate rules for costal shipping and ships going abroad, financial relief to cargo carrying vessels to help increase sea-related trade traffic and income tax benefits to coastal shipping.
Business Standard
FOREIGN DIRECT INVESTMENT ALLOWED IN PREFERENCE SHARES

The Finance Ministry on Thursday decided to allow Indian companies to raise foreign capital through preference shares. Such investments will be treated as part of share capital and not as debt. External commercial borrowing rules will not be applicable to such investments.

But it will be permitted only as rupee-denominated instruments in accordance with the Companies Act, 1956. Since preference shares will be treated as equity, all foreign investments flowing in through this route will be treated as foreign direct investment.
The companies will either have to seek Reserve Bank clearances under the automatic approval window or apply to the Foreign Investment Promotion Board for a case by case clearance.
18 SEAFOOD UNITS ELIGIBLE FOR EXPORT TO EUROPEAN UNION

The Commerce Ministry has identified 18 seafood exporting units which meet the strict hygiene standards set by the European Union and are eligible to export their products to the European Union. In a letter to the Union's vice president, the Indian commerce minister on Thursday urged the European Union to continue imports from these 18 units.

The minister promised to suspend exports by all units that fail to meet the hygiene requirements. The European Union has recommended a ban on seafood import from India unless the stringent hygiene requirements set by it are not met.
SOAP GIANTS BACK HINDUSTAN LEVER IN TRADE BATTLE

A number of multi-national companies and domestic companies in the soaps and toiletries segment are supporting Hindustan Lever whose products are being boycotted by the traders in Kerala state. The traders are demanding a rise in commission.

The Indian Soaps and Toiletry Manufacturers' Association has decided to back Hindustan Lever (HLL) and will meet the state chief minister soon. The association has also decided to take legal action against stockists supporting the boycott.
HLL sources said companies like Proctor and Gamble, Nirma and Godrej Soaps had decided to fight the traders in Kerala. They also said they had the support of the Tata Tea company.
The Observer
GOVERNMENT FIRMS MONOPOLISE RESOURCE MOBILISATION
The government has monopolised the resource mobilisation from the primary capital market specially after investors lost faith in the private sector in the last two financial years.
According to Prime which is India's premier data base on the primary capital market, the public sectors share in the total resource mobilisation equalled 75.39 billion rupees in 1996/97.

This was only 12.51 billion rupees (9 pct) in 1994/95 and 50.59 billion rupees (43 pct) in 1995/96. The state-owned companies mustered 87 percent of the total 99.17 billion rupees mobilised through debt public issues during fiscal 1996/97.
